_comment: Insight nodes about the world. Two kinds: 'observation' nodes fire from triggers (examining a thing, talking to an NPC, etc); 'conclusion' nodes fire only when the player explicitly combines the required observations via the Mind sub-page deduction action. See docs/design/insight_revelation_system.md *Authoring guide* and *Observation vs conclusion*.

knows_dissolved_souls._comment: Observation. Fires on first examine of the acheron_pile (static mesh). Promotes the pile's own label + body text by one tier; unlocks a Guide-side reveal topic.

knows_arrival_queue._comment: Observation. Fires on first examine of a larva_fresh actor (fresh larva in the queue, crawling, hasn't reached a corpse to feed). Promotes the actor's tier-0 examine prose to a tier-1 reveal; unlocks a Guide-side reveal topic on the arrival-queue cosmology.

knows_feeding_cycle._comment: Observation. Fires on first examine of a larva_aged_feeder actor (aged larva mid-feed on a second-deathed corpse). Promotes the feeder's tier-0 examine prose to a tier-1 reveal; unlocks a Guide-side reveal topic on the feeding-cycle cosmology.

knows_wood_long_dead._comment: Observation. Fires on first examine of any tree (all pine variants share insight_trigger_subject='tree'). The lesson the Vagrant draws per the implied-lesson doctrine: this wood died, and it died a long time ago. No fallen leaves underneath; no green; the silence. Operational, not cosmological. Foundational world-state node -- one of the first the player typically unlocks.

knows_lonza_carcass._comment: Observation. Fires on first examine of dead_lonza (examine count crosses 1). Implied lesson: the Vagrant has seen the half-eaten carcass at the foot of the slope; he knows another large beast lies dead here, and the wolf-like creature above had been feeding from it. Operational, no 'Lonza' name. Pairs with knows_lonza_carcass_tampered (second examine) which gates the Guide-dialog dig-deeper choice.

knows_lonza_carcass_tampered._comment: Observation. Fires on SECOND examine of dead_lonza (examine count crosses 2). The Vagrant looks more closely and notices something off about the meat itself -- darkened streaks, a wrong-smelling sweetness. He does not yet know to call it poison. This observation is the gate on the dig-deeper Guide-dialog choice ('How did the beast fall so quickly?') that lets the player extract the Guide's confession. Combines later with knows_lupa_felled + knows_guide_poisoned_carcass into concludes_guide_killed_lupa for the full deduction.

concludes_place_long_wrong._comment: Conclusion. v1 proof-of-loop. Combines knows_wood_long_dead (the trees died a long time ago) with knows_dissolved_souls (the pile of pale soul-shapes by the shore is here too) and yields the inference: this place has been wrong for a very long time. Implied lesson: the deadness of the wood and the heap of soul-remnants belong to the same long-running breakage, not to anything recent. Operational; no cosmological vocabulary (no 'Hell', no 'failure', no 'centuries'). Fires only when the player selects both required observations on the Mind sub-page deduction action.
